source_integrity.summary: Seventeen numbered institutional and research references per locale with 17/17 declared citations, no missing reference labels. High-impact numerical claims checked against Stanford HAI, IMF, IEA, NBER, IBGE, ILO and Anthropic public primary records.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: 2023 and 2025 adoption survey observations, 2024 IMF exposure estimates, IEA observed 2024 versus projected 2030 consumption, 2026 labor papers, Sep 2026 executive positions and September 2026 IBGE moving-quarter observation released 30 Oct are separately dated.

factual_methodology.summary: No observed layoffs inferred from task exposure. Corporate speeches explicitly attributed; observed, estimated, projected and possible states separated. 2026 September Brazil unemployment 5.2% rechecked with IBGE and official government report.

research_depth.summary: English around 5,415 substantive words and Portuguese around 5,877, each in 15 connected sections; AI adoption, labor, entry-level recruitment, ownership, UBI financing, Brazilian constraints, defense, psychology and counter-hypotheses covered.

evidence_traceability.summary: 17 numbered references in each language across 14 distinct domains, citations mapped to source list; primary claims include Stanford 2025 survey 88% and 2023 55%; IMF 60/40/26 exposure estimates; IEA 2024 415 TWh versus 2030 Base Case 945 TWh; observed IBGE Sep 2026 5.2%.

counterfactual_review.summary: Four observable conditional interpretations and explicit falsifiers; distinguishes task exposure from unemployment, experiment from national UBI, energy scenario from historical demand, and military programme from operational effectiveness.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Three explicitly sourced bar charts in both locales with matching numeric sequences 55/88, 60/40/26 and 415/945; one causal flow, one regional map and four analytical tables per language. Observed vs. forecast status disclosed, no synthetic map coordinates.

bilingual_equivalence.summary: All 15 analytic sections, material quantities, 17-reference bibliography, labels, institutional attributions, uncertainty caveats and scenarios retained in Portuguese; chart values parity verified.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: No internal tool-build or QA narration in public manuscripts; editorial lint patterns examined with no matches, original manuscript SHA files read after final source updates, candidate not previously public and kind registered in active system-registry.

contrary_evidence: Observed AI use and rising model capability do not imply a causal unemployment increase; ILO and Anthropic find limited aggregate displacement to date.
Cash-transfer experiment provides evidence of labour supply adjustment, not a general verdict on universal basic income financed under other conditions.
Benchmark improvement does not establish firm-level productive output or durable market power; open competition and institutional adaptation remain credible alternatives.
limitations: No complete repository-local npm run validate or npm run build executed in this review environment; GitHub Actions must validate before production deployment.
Not every external article URL was re-fetched line by line; selected highest-risk numbers, dates and source identities were independently cross-checked.
Psychological findings are provisional and heterogeneous; the APA summary includes studies of different designs, some not peer reviewed.
Approval constitutes an editorial consistency and source-traceability assessment, not certification of every empirical forecast or endorsement of any ideology.
notes: QA review completed as a separate verification pass after bilingual drafting. No changes were made to reviewed manuscripts during this approval. Approval is bound to exact pending and source Git blobs; the publisher must reverify them and reconcile cumulative systems before promotion.

en.title: After Accelerationism: Artificial Intelligence, Labour Income and the Struggle over the Pace of the Twenty-First Century
en.deck: Why accelerating AI capability does not automatically produce broad prosperity: employment, early-career opportunity, capital ownership, basic income, electrical infrastructure, governance and autonomous warfare under 2026 evidence.
en.regime: Fast technical diffusion, contested labour effects and unequal infrastructures.
en.key_risk: Mistaking task exposure for unemployment, announced capital expenditure for delivered productivity and corporate statements for verified policy outcomes.
watch: Youth hiring and employment in exposed occupations
Cost per verified task and measured firm-level productivity
Worker income share and cloud/chip concentration
